payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the mug to the right of the headphones
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: In the edited image, is the mug corresponding to the mug in the source image positioned to the right of the headphones, and does the visual evidence establish whether the requested move is complete?
node.criteria: Pass only if the source mug can be identified by visual correspondence in the edited image and is visibly to the right of the headphones, with the requested move complete. Fail if the corresponding source mug is identifiable and the requested move has not been made. Unknown if the mug's identity, its relation to the headphones, or completion of the requested move cannot be determined from the source and edited images; do not infer completion merely because another mug is to the right of the headphones.
node.binding: Compare the source image's blue mug with objects in the edited image to identify its corresponding mug, then compare that mug's position with the headphones in the edited image. Consider all visible mug-like objects; if correspondence or completion is ambiguous, use unknown.

node_traces.evidence: The source contains a distinctive blue mug to the left of the headphones. In the edited image, there are two mug-like objects: a pale mug near the left side of the headphones and a mug to their right. Neither visibly matches the source mug's blue appearance, and the source mug may be absent or altered; the correspondence cannot be established confidently, so it is unclear whether the requested move is complete.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is truncated/underspecified (“objects in (...)”) and should explicitly anchor the comparison to the source and edited images and the requested move. The trace identifies a pale mug near the headphones and another to their right, but treats color mismatch as preventing correspondence and overlooks the strong spatial/shape evidence: the source blue mug appears as a blue, blurred remnant at the far left, while the edited image also contains mug-like objects on both sides of the headphones. Assess whether the original mug remains at its source location and whether either candidate plausibly represents it; distinguish evidence of partial movement from evidence that the move is complete. Do not equate any mug right of the headphones with the source mug, or infer absence solely from altered color/appearance. Preserve unknown when correspondence genuinely cannot be resolved, but make the criterion state how to evaluate partial progress and completion separately so the node does not collapse ambiguity into unresolved. The high-confidence unknown is a visual-criterion/calibration issue, not a transport or dependency failure; the aggregate reference label “partial” is a constraint, not atomic ground truth."}
